notes: Machine-readable mirror of technique-mapping-table.md. If the two ever disagree, technique-mapping-table.md is the source of truth and this file should be regenerated from it — do not hand-edit this file independently.

global_rules.selection_when_over_cap: rank by detection_confidence descending, keep top N up to cap

entries.instruction_template: Deepen the eyeliner slightly at the inner corner to visually narrow the distance between the eyes.
Create a clearly visible but fine tapered wing from the outer third of the upper lash line, lifting it upward and outward; leave visible skin between pigment and the eye opening.
Slightly thicken the eyeliner along the lash line so it remains visible when the eye is open.
Extend the eyeliner outward toward the outer corner; keep the inner corner thin or bare.
Trace a fine tapered line along the outer third of the upper lash line and lift its tip slightly; keep the inner corner soft.
Apply a light highlight tone to the center of the upper lid to soften shadow depth.
Build clearly visible, blended depth at the outer corner and outer crease, keeping pigment above and outside the visible eye opening.
Blend a slightly deeper tone into the inner corner to narrow the visual gap.
Extend eyeshadow blending toward the outer corner; keep inner corner light.
Shift the eyeshadow hue slightly toward the warm or cool direction that harmonizes with the skin undertone (small relative hue delta, capped per color_adjustment_caps).
Shift the eyeshadow hue slightly toward the complement of the iris color so the eyes stand out (small relative hue delta, capped per color_adjustment_caps).
Blend a soft midtone over the outer third of the upper lid, fading gently upward while leaving the inner lid light.

visibility_precondition.note: skip whole region if either brow is occluded (bangs, glasses, hat, hand)

entries.instruction_template: Deepen the brow color slightly relative to its current value (small relative lightness delta, capped) so the brows frame the eyes more clearly.
Lighten the brow color slightly toward the hair color (small relative lightness delta, capped) to soften a harsh look.
Shift the brow hue slightly toward the hair hue (small relative hue delta, capped) so brow and hair read as harmonious.
Fill sparse gaps inside the existing brow outline with fine hair-like strokes that match the existing hair color and growth direction. Do not extend beyond the current brow boundary.
Define the brow tail by extending it slightly along its existing direction (capped extension). Keep the tail angle unchanged.
Slightly sharpen the lower edge of the brow so its shape reads more clearly, without moving the edge.
Fill or define only the weaker brow slightly so the pair looks more balanced. Do not move either brow's position or arch.
entries.enabled_note: ships disabled by default — highest identity-drift risk of the brow entries; enable only after Phase 1 confirms no landmark drift beyond tolerance on the diverse test set

entries.instruction_template: Add a few soft, hairlike strokes only within the existing brow to make it read a little fuller and groomed. Follow its natural growth direction and preserve its outline; do not sharpen the lower edge or impose a straight or arched shape.
Increase lip color saturation/brightness relative to its current detected value (relative delta, not a fixed target shade).
Add a very thin highlight to the center of the lower lip to suggest fullness, without altering lip outline.
Shift the lip color hue slightly toward a shade that harmonizes with the skin undertone (small relative hue delta, capped per color_adjustment_caps). Keep lightness roughly unchanged.

trigger.note: lip chroma relative to eye-region and cheek chroma

entries.instruction_template: Reduce lip color saturation slightly relative to its current value so it balances with the rest of the look.

excluded.would_be_trigger: lip peak / cupid's bow not well-defined
excluded.reason: Borders on altering facial geometry rather than applying makeup color/technique — conflicts with the no-facial-feature-reshaping rule (Section 5 of the main design doc). Do not add without revisiting that rule explicitly.

nose_contour.risk_note: Higher risk than eyeliner/eyeshadow/lips — contouring can read as reshaping if overdone. intensity should default lower than other regions; Section 19 validation should weight this region's outside-mask/edge checks more strictly.

entries.instruction_template: Apply a very subtle shadow along both sides of the nose to visually narrow its width. Keep effect minimal.
Apply a thin highlight down the center of the nose bridge to add dimension.
Apply soft cheek color at the placement specified for the selected style, adapted to the visible face and blended without a hard edge or round patch.

foundation.scope_constraint: Local highlight/concealer points only, never full-face tone-matching, smoothing, or blemish removal. A full-face mask conflicts with the localized-edit architecture (Section 17) and sharply raises identity-drift risk. Treat 'even out skin tone across the whole face' as a separate, unapproved scope discussion if ever requested.

entries.instruction_template: Apply light, localized concealer-style brightening strictly within the under-eye shadow area.
Add a small amount of highlight at the top of the cheekbone and down the nose bridge center.
